name.text: Rewriting an equation in logarithmic form

questiontext.text:
Rewrite the following equation in logarithmic form. \( {@a@}^{@n@}={@b@} \) Enter your answer as a logarithmic equation.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Recall the relationship between index form and logarithmic form:

\( a^n=b \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \log_a(b)=n. \)

In this question, the given equation is

\( {@a@}^{@n@}={@b@}. \)

To rewrite this equation in logarithmic form, follow these steps:

1. The base of the power, {@a@}, becomes the base of the logarithm.

2. The result of the power, {@b@}, becomes the argument of the logarithm.

3. The exponent, {@n@}, becomes the value of the logarithm.

Therefore, the equivalent logarithmic equation is

\( \log_{@a@}(@b@)=@n@. \)

Remember that logarithms answer the question: “To what power must the base be raised to obtain the given number?”

Example: If the question displays \({@3@}^{@4@}=81\), then the equivalent logarithmic form is

\( \log_3(81)=4. \)
